s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness in a pregnant woman with persistent symptoms and abnormal laboratory tests
key_facts: initially diagnosed with upper respiratory tract infection
normal urine and liver function tests

raw.syndrome_frame: febrile illness in a pregnant woman with persistent symptoms and abnormal laboratory tests
key_facts: initially diagnosed with upper respiratory tract infection
normal urine and liver function tests

shortlist.label: Listeriosis
shortlist.why_kept: positive blood culture and persistent fever in a pregnant woman

shortlist.label: Pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: fever and elevated CRP in a pregnant woman

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: persistent fever, elevated CRP and PCT, and positive blood culture

shortlist.label: Urinary tract infection
shortlist.why_kept: fever and elevated CRP in a pregnant woman, although urine tests are normal

shortlist.label: Influenza
shortlist.why_kept: initial diagnosis of upper respiratory tract infection and persistent fever

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive blood culture and persistent fever despite initial diagnosis of upper respiratory tract infection, which are key indicators of Listeriosis, especially in a pregnant woman. The normal urine and liver function tests and negative vaginal swabs also point away from other infections like Pyelonephritis or Urinary tract infection.

rejected.label: Pyelonephritis
rejected.why: Normal urine tests do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Sepsis
rejected.why: While the patient has a fever and positive blood culture, the specific identification of serovars and MLST analysis suggest a more specific infection like Listeriosis

rejected.label: Urinary tract infection
rejected.why: Vaginal swabs were negative for pathogens and urine tests were normal

rejected.label: Influenza
rejected.why: The positive blood culture and specific serotyping results do not align with a viral infection like Influenza
